title: Gold Market Primer: Market size and structure
gist: The World Gold Council maps a US$31tn above-ground gold market (~220,700t) in which investable gold exceeds US$15tn and central banks hold 38,600t worth US$5tn. It argues gold remains structurally under-allocated at ~3% of global financial assets (versus ~14% forty years ago), while record US$361bn/day liquidity and rising official-sector demand reshape the market.

themes.theme: Market size and above-ground stock composition

insights.claim: The total above-ground gold stock is roughly 220,700t valued at approximately US$31tn as of end-2025, growing only ~1.8% per year through newly mined metal.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The near-fixed ~1.8% annual supply growth means demand-side investment flows, not new mine output, drive price at the margin — a structural bull case for gold in any allocation-shift scenario.
insights.quote: The stock also grows slowly – by around 1.8% per year through newly mined metal – reinforcing gold's scarcity over time.
insights.locator: The stock also grows slowly

insights.claim: Jewellery accounts for 45% of above-ground gold (99,700t, US$14tn), bars and coins 21% (47,000t, US$7tn), central banks 17% (38,600t, US$5tn), technology and other industrial uses 10% (21,400t, US$3tn), OTC institutional/HNW holdings ~5% (up to 10,000t, US$1.4tn), and gold ETFs 2% (4,000t, US$0.6tn).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The stock breakdown shows a large latent pool — jewellery plus OTC — that can be mobilised as recycled supply or investment flow, cushioning shocks and setting the real float available to price-sensitive buyers.
insights.quote: Jewellery accounts for 45% (99,700t, US$14tn) Central banks and other official institutions hold 17% (38,600t, US$5tn) as reserves
insights.locator: A useful way to visualise this is the 'gold cube'

insights.claim: Because gold is virtually indestructible, historical production persists as potential inventory, so the market is determined by a large existing stock that responds to price, risk and preferences rather than by new mine production alone.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indestructibility means gold has no depletion cycle like other commodities; secondary-market mobilisation of stock is the key swing variable to watch for supply response.
insights.quote: Gold is virtually indestructible, so unlike many industrial commodities, historical production continues to exist as potential inventory in some form
insights.locator: Importantly, the stock is permanent

insights.claim: Gold reserves (economically extractable) are estimated at ~66,000t by the US Geological Survey, a fraction of the ~220,700t already above ground.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Underground economically-extractable reserves (~66,000t) are dwarfed by above-ground stock, reinforcing that recycling and stock mobilisation, not mining, set the effective supply ceiling.
insights.quote: reserves are currently estimated to be ~66,000t by the US Geological Survey
insights.locator: Reserves are the portion of an ore deposit

insights.claim: The total investable gold market is worth more than US$15tn — over US$9tn in bars, coins, ETFs and OTC held by private investors, US$5tn managed by central banks and official institutions, and nearly US$1.5tn in derivatives.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A US$15tn+ investable pool with US$9tn in private hands shows enough depth to absorb large institutional reallocation without dislocation — capacity is not the constraint on higher allocations.
insights.quote: investable gold, mostly in bullion form, amounts to more than US$15tn
insights.locator: A deep and diverse financial market

insights.claim: The total financial physical gold market (bars, coins, ETFs, central bank reserves, OTC) is worth about US$14tn and totals around 100,000t, representing roughly 45% of all above-ground gold stocks.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Nearly half of all mined gold sits in explicitly financial/reserve form, meaning gold's price is set as much by monetary and investment demand as by consumer jewellery use.
insights.quote: these segments – bars, coins, ETFs, central bank reserves and OTC investments – constitute the total financial physical gold market, with a value of approximately US$14tn
insights.locator: Central bank reserves also play a significant role

insights.claim: Gold derivatives open interest (futures and options) was worth around US$1.5tn at end-2025 — a small fraction of physical holdings — yet daily volumes reached US$114bn on COMEX and US$51bn on the Shanghai Futures Exchange.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A relatively small derivatives book (US$1.5tn) generating outsized daily turnover means price discovery is concentrated in futures; the small notional relative to physical keeps systemic leverage low versus other markets.
insights.quote: Average daily trading volumes in 2025 reached US$114bn on COMEX and US$51bn on the Shanghai Futures Exchange.
insights.locator: At the end of 2025 derivatives open interest

insights.claim: OTC gold holdings by institutions and high net worth investors are estimated as high as 10,000t (a 5,000-10,000t range), largely invisible because they represent private off-exchange positions.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A hidden pool of up to 10,000t means published positioning data understates true institutional exposure; flow surprises can come from this opaque segment.
insights.quote: OTC holdings, estimated to as high as 10,000t, represent positions acquired through private transactions rather than on exchanges, rendering them less visible
insights.locator: In addition, OTC gold investment stands out

insights.claim: Global gold trading averaged a record US$361bn per day in 2025 — equivalent to 3,000t changing hands daily — split between US$180-187bn/day OTC in London and ~US$174bn/day on exchanges.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Record daily turnover confirms institutional-grade liquidity, meaning large allocators can enter or exit at scale — removing a common objection to sizing gold like a core reserve asset.
insights.quote: gold traded a record US$361bn per day on average in 2025, equivalent to 3,000t exchanging hands daily
insights.locator: Institutional-grade liquidity

insights.claim: In 2025 London OTC gold volumes were significantly higher than UK Gilts and German Bunds and broadly in line with 7-10 year US Treasuries and T-bills.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold trading rivals sovereign bond markets in depth, supporting its case as a genuine reserve/liquidity asset — particularly valuable because liquidity holds up during financial stress when other markets seize.
insights.quote: In 2025 London OTC volumes alone were significantly higher than comparable statistics for UK Gilts and German Bunds, and broadly in line with 7–10 year US Treasuries and T-bills
insights.locator: Few financial assets can match the gold market's liquidity

insights.claim: COMEX leads gold derivatives trading, followed by the fast-growing Shanghai Futures Exchange, while London remains the key OTC hub with more than US$160bn in daily over-the-counter volumes, mostly spot.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The rise of Shanghai signals eastward migration of price-setting activity; watch SHFE growth as a barometer of Chinese demand influence on global gold pricing.
insights.quote: COMEX leads in derivatives trading, followed by the fast-growing Shanghai Futures Exchange
insights.locator: Institutional-grade liquidity

insights.claim: Gold bullion held by investors (~US$9tn in bars, coins, ETFs and OTC) is only 3% of the estimated US$320tn invested in global financial assets, down from around 14% roughly 40 years ago.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The gap between today's 3% share and the historical ~14% frames the core bull thesis: even a partial reversion toward prior allocation levels implies trillions of incremental demand against a slow-growing stock.
insights.quote: the ~US$9tn of gold bullion held by individual and institutional investors (bars, coins, gold ETFs and OTC) accounts for 3% of the estimated US$320tn invested in financial assets globally
insights.locator: We estimate that the ~US$9tn

insights.claim: Up to 30% of investors may hold no allocation to gold at all, and institutions in particular tend to be significantly under-allocated.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A large cohort of zero-allocation and under-allocated institutions represents latent demand; marginal shifts from this base can move a slow-supply market meaningfully.
insights.quote: up to 30% of investors may not have any allocation to gold. And among those investors who do hold gold, institutions in particular tend, on average, to be significantly under‑allocated
insights.locator: But gold holdings are not uniform across portfolios

insights.claim: The WGC's analysis of USD portfolios from end-2005 to end-2025 shows a 5% strategic gold allocation (range 2-10%) improved risk-adjusted returns in a well-balanced portfolio, with higher optimal allocations for markets like India or Japan.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Provides a concrete allocation target (2-10%, centered on 5%) to benchmark portfolios against; the gap between this and actual near-zero holdings is the actionable positioning signal.
insights.quote: investors can benefit from a 5% strategic allocation in a well-balanced portfolio, with a range between 2% to 10% depending on their investment objectives
insights.locator: In contrast, our analysis shows

insights.claim: Gold represents 3% of global financial assets excluding central bank reserves, but its distribution is highly uneven, leaving it significantly under-allocated across many portfolios.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The uneven distribution means aggregate averages mask deep pockets of zero exposure, so allocation-driven demand can be lumpy and concentrated rather than smooth.
insights.quote: gold makes up 3% of global financial assets (excluding central bank reserves); however, it is not uniformly distributed and remains significantly under‑allocated in many investor portfolios
insights.locator: An under-owned strategic investment

insights.claim: Central banks and official institutions hold over 38,000t of gold worth US$5tn, equal to 26% of global allocated reserves in 2025, rising to 29% of total allocated reserves by Q1 2026 per IMF COFER — second only to the US dollar.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold overtaking all reserve currencies except USD marks a structural regime; the official sector is now a durable price-insensitive buyer, a key support beneath the market.
insights.quote: By Q1 2026 gold accounted for 29% of total global allocated reserves, according to IMF COFER data, with only the US dollar holding a greater share
insights.locator: At the end of 2025 central banks held approximately 38,600t

insights.claim: Developed-market central banks held on average 30% of reserves in gold in 2025 versus just 15% for emerging markets, up from around 4% for EM in 2010 after which EM demand expanded rapidly.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The EM catch-up from 4% (2010) to 15% toward the DM 30% level implies years of structural official buying still ahead — the single most important sustained demand driver to track.
insights.quote: in 2025 developed market central banks held, on average, 30% of their total reserves in gold. In comparison, their emerging market counterparts held just 15%; this compares with around 4% in 2010
insights.locator: However, there can be a sizeable divergence

insights.claim: In the WGC 2026 central bank survey, 74% of respondents expected moderate or significantly lower US dollar holdings in global reserves over the next five years, while expecting the euro, renminbi and gold shares to stay the same or increase.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A 74% majority of reserve managers signalling dollar reduction is direct forward guidance on multi-year official gold demand and de-dollarisation — a core macro tailwind.
insights.quote: the majority of respondents (74%) expected moderate or significantly lower US dollar holdings within global reserves over the next five years
insights.locator: Our survey also found that the majority

insights.claim: The WGC 2026 central bank survey identifies gold's crisis performance, its effectiveness as a diversifier, and its long-term store of value as the key drivers behind central bank gold ownership.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: These motivations are structural rather than tactical, implying official demand is relatively price-insensitive and unlikely to reverse on short-term price moves.
insights.quote: gold's performance during times of crisis, its effectiveness as a diversifier, and its long-term store of value are key drivers behind gold ownership
insights.locator: Why do central banks hold so much gold?

insights.claim: As of Q1 2026 the composition of total allocated reserves was 40% USD, 29% gold, 14% EUR, 15% others and 1% CNY.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold at 29% now exceeds the euro's 14% and dwarfs the renminbi's 1%, showing metal — not a rival fiat currency — is the dollar's main diversification alternative for reserve managers.
insights.quote: 40%14%1%29%15%USDEURCNYGoldOthers
insights.locator: Chart 6: Gold is a key component

themes.theme: Supply-demand diversity and the dual nature framework

insights.claim: Gold supply is roughly 75% mined and 25% recycled (2016-2025 average), with no single region producing more than a quarter of global mine output, so recycling acts as a buffer that fills gaps when primary production cannot meet demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Geographically diffuse mining plus a large recyclable stock limits supply shocks and dampens volatility versus concentrated commodities — a stability argument for reserve and portfolio use.
insights.quote: gold is supplied from a mix of mined (75%) and recycled (25%) sources.
insights.locator: Supply: gold is supplied from a mix

insights.claim: Emerging markets, dominated by China and India, represent around 50% of annual global gold demand (2016-2025 average), with developed markets accounting for the remainder.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Half of demand originating in China and India ties gold's consumer flows to EM income growth and monsoon/wedding-season cycles — a demand base structurally distinct from Western investment flows.
insights.quote: Emerging markets – dominated by China and India – represent around 50% of annual global gold demand, while developed markets account for the remainder.
insights.locator: Demand: gold is bought around the world

insights.claim: Gold's demand splits into consumer use — jewellery 29% and technology 6% — and investment use — investment 43% and central banks 21% — on average annual net demand of approximately US$351bn (10-year average to 2025).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The ~64% investment-plus-official share versus ~35% consumer share quantifies gold's dual nature and shows financial/monetary demand now dominates the annual flow that sets price.
insights.quote: consumer use – jewellery (29%) and technology (6%) – and investment use – investment (43%) and central banks (21%)
insights.locator: Gold has a diverse demand base

insights.claim: Gold's dual nature means pro-cyclical consumer demand supports it during economic expansion while counter-cyclical investment demand rises during uncertainty and can drive the price higher, so different drivers dominate at different points in the cycle.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: This framework explains gold's low correlation to other assets across regimes; investors should watch which demand engine is active — consumer income growth versus macro risk — to time exposure.
insights.quote: During periods of economic expansion, pro‑cyclical consumer demand can support gold's performance. During periods of economic uncertainty, counter‑cyclical investment demand tends to rise and can drive the gold price higher.
insights.locator: In practical terms, this dual nature

insights.claim: Net demand figures use the 2025 annual average LBMA Gold Price PM of US$3,431.5/oz.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A 2025 average gold price above US$3,400/oz anchors the dollar values throughout and marks the elevated price regime underpinning the US$31tn stock valuation.
insights.quote: US dollar value computed using the 2025 annual average LBMA Gold Price PM of US$3,431.5/oz.
insights.locator: Based on 10-year average annual net demand

insights.claim: Four structural developments reshaped gold demand over the past 30 years: EM economic growth, the advent of physically-backed gold ETFs, the re-emergence of central bank net buying since late 2009, and the Global Financial Crisis cementing gold as a liquid diversifier.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: These four forces broadened the demand base, reducing single-sector dependence; each remains active, suggesting the structural demand story is durable rather than cyclical.
insights.quote: Re-emergence of central bank demand: Since late 2009, central banks have returned as sustained net buyers, seeking diversification, liquidity and crisis protection
insights.locator: Four key structural developments underpin this transformation

insights.claim: A broader, more diverse demand base reduces the market's dependence on any single sector and helps it adjust when one source of demand weakens, which supports overall market stability.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Diversified demand implies lower drawdown risk from any one buyer group retreating — a stability feature relevant when sizing gold as a strategic rather than tactical holding.
insights.quote: A broader demand base can reduce dependence on a single sector and can help the market adjust when one source of demand weakens.
insights.locator: This evolution matters for market stability
